raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

In a DSv4.1 DEP16 decode trace with DSpark verify (bs 256 per rank), building the indexer metadata for the ratio-1 and ratio-2 layers ran a chain of torch ops for each ratio: int64 cast, multiply, broadcast add of an arange, and a cast back to int32. All of them ran at the full expanded width, `[1024, 2049 * blocks_per_page]`. Together they took about 67 µs per step.

## Modifications

- `expand_index_page_table` (`dsv4/metadata.py`) sends GPU tables with unit column stride and a power-of-two `blocks_per_page` to the existing Triton kernel in `attn_glue_hip.py`. That kernel writes the int32 table in one launch and matches the torch expression bit for bit. Other inputs keep the torch path.
- `test_dsv41_decode_glue_hip.py::test_expand_index_page_table` used `expand_index_page_table` as its reference. After this change it would compare the Triton kernel with itself, so its reference now runs the torch expression on CPU.
- `test_fp4_indexer.py::test_expand_index_page_table_matches_cpu` (CUDA) covers the CUDA dispatch, which the gfx95-gated HIP file does not. It compares the GPU result with the CPU torch path, on a contiguous and a row-strided table.

## Accuracy Tests

Output is bitwise identical. A standalone check on one GPU compared the Triton kernel with the previous torch expression using `torch.equal` on these inputs:
- `[1024, 2049]` with `blocks_per_page` 4 and 2
- `[256, 2049]`, `[3, 17]`, `[1, 300]` and an empty table
- a row-strided table
- `-1` entries and int32 edge values (`2^31 - 1`, `-2^31`, `2^30`)

All matched. `test_expand_index_page_table_matches_cpu` passes on a B300 (5/5).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Each call was captured in a CUDA graph and replayed 200 times, in A/B/A/B order. Times include the graph-replay overhead.

| shape | blocks_per_page | before (µs) | after (µs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[1024, 2049]` | 4 (ratio 1) | 40.9 / 41.1 | 7.1 / 7.2 |
| `[1024, 2049]` | 2 (ratio 2) | 25.0 / 26.7 | 7.3 / 7.1 |

That is about 67 → 14 µs per decode step at bs 256. Prefill and the sparse-candidate table use the same function, so they benefit too. These numbers come from running the operation alone; end-to-end step time was not measured.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -406,6 +406,16 @@ def expand_index_page_table(
     blocks_per_page = slots_per_page // index_page_size
     if blocks_per_page == 1:
         return page_table
+    if (
+        page_table.is_cuda
+        and page_table.stride(1) == 1
+        and blocks_per_page & (blocks_per_page - 1) == 0
+    ):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.attn_glue_hip import (
+            expand_index_page_table as expand_index_page_table_triton,
+        )
+
+        return expand_index_page_table_triton(page_table, blocks_per_page)
     bs, n = page_table.shape
     base = page_table.to(torch.int64) * blocks_per_page
     offsets = torch.arange(blocks_per_page, device=page_table.device, dtype=torch.int64)

@@ -284,8 +284,11 @@ def test_expand_index_page_table(bpp: int):
             0, 1 << 20, (bs, n), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE
         )
         ref = _expand_index_page_table(
-            page_table, full_page_size=64 * bpp, compress_ratio=1, index_page_size=64
-        )
+            page_table.cpu(),
+            full_page_size=64 * bpp,
+            compress_ratio=1,
+            index_page_size=64,
+        ).to(DEVICE)
         out = expand_index_page_table(page_table, bpp)
         assert out.dtype is torch.int32 and out.shape == ref.shape
         assert torch.equal(out, ref)
@@ -296,8 +299,8 @@ def test_expand_index_page_table(bpp: int):
     assert torch.equal(
         expand_index_page_table(page_table, 4),
         _expand_index_page_table(
-            page_table, full_page_size=256, compress_ratio=1, index_page_size=64
-        ),
+            page_table.cpu(), full_page_size=256, compress_ratio=1, index_page_size=64
+        ).to(DEVICE),
     )

@@ -627,6 +627,31 @@ def run():
                 assert (out.raw_indices[batch] == -1).all().item()
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "bs,n,bpp",
+    [(1024, 2049, 4), (1024, 2049, 2), (3, 17, 2), (0, 10, 4), (5, 9, 3)],
+)
+def test_expand_index_page_table_matches_cpu(bs, n, bpp):
+    """The GPU expansion is bitwise the torch expression the CPU path runs; bpp 3
+    stays on torch."""
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsv4.metadata import expand_index_page_table
+
+    def expand(t):
+        return expand_index_page_table(
+            t, full_page_size=64 * bpp, compress_ratio=1, index_page_size=64
+        )
+
+    torch.manual_seed(bs + n + bpp)
+    t = torch.randint(0, 1 << 20, (2 * bs, n), device=get_device(), dtype=torch.int32)
+    if bs and n >= 8:
+        t[:, -3:] = -1
+        t[0, :4] = t.new_tensor([2**31 - 1, 2**30, 2**29 + 7, -(2**31)])
+    for table in (t[:bs], t[::2]):
+        out = expand(table)
+        assert out.dtype == torch.int32
+        assert torch.equal(out.cpu(), expand(table.cpu()))
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [0, 1, 32, 129])
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("topk", [0, 1, 65, 512])
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("write_raw", [False, True])
